apps.name: Meeting Notes
apps.tagline: Capture every meeting, forget nothing
apps.description:
Capture and understand your meetings with automatic recording, transcription, and summarization all in one place.

Uses Gemini API which you can get for free usage with no subscription costs.  Always pulls the lates Gemini Flash model.

Requires you download local whisper ai so you don’t have to pay for that either.

Key Features:
- Record meetings directly from your desktop and access transcripts instantly
- Summarize long conversations into key takeaways and action items
- Browse your entire meeting history and search through transcripts
- Configure your preferred transcription settings and models in one place

SETUP INSTRUCTIONS

1. Get a Google Gemini API key (required for AI summaries)

Sign up at Google AI Studio, generate an API key, paste it into the app's Settings screen. It's stored encrypted on-device.

2. Set up transcription (pick one path)

Easy path: Install Homebrew if not already installed, then use the app's one-click "Install" button in Settings to install whisper-cpp + ffmpeg, then download a Whisper model (e.g. "base.en") from the same screen.
Advanced path: Already have Whisper (whisper.cpp or OpenAI Whisper) installed elsewhere (e.g. on iCloud Drive)? Point Settings at that custom binary + model file instead — no Homebrew needed. ffmpeg is still required from Homebrew/PATH either way (used to convert recordings to 16kHz WAV).

3. Grant macOS permissions

Microphone — for recording their voice.
Screen Recording — required to capture system/meeting-participant audio (macOS will prompt; if skipped, the app still works but falls back to mic-only recording). Also needs macOS 14.2+ for system audio capture.

4. That's it — start recording

The app has a built-in "setup gate" that only unlocks recording once Whisper + ffmpeg + a model are ready, and shows exactly what's still missing if not.
No manual config file editing or account creation beyond the Gemini key — everything else is one-click or automatic inside the app.

Most finance trackers live in the cloud. Family Vault does not. There is no server, no sync, no account required, and no company that can ever see your data. Everything stays encrypted on your own Mac, protected by a master password and Touch ID, the same way a bank vault protects what matters.

Here’s what you get

- A flexible Holdings tracker for savings accounts, fixed deposits, stocks, 401(k)s and IRAs, mutual funds, life and health insurance, property, mortgages, and more, fully customizable to any country's account types.
- A dashboard with a genuinely commanding net worth figure, correctly separating insurance cover from real assets, broken down by person and by asset type with intensity-scaled bars that make big and small holdings visually obvious.
- Coming Up alerts for maturities, renewals, and premiums, with real macOS Reminders so you're alerted even when the app is fully closed.
- One click demo data, so you can explore the whole app with a realistic fictional family before entering anything of your own.
- Fully custom fields, your own text, number, date, dropdown, or yes/no fields on any holding, with sort, filter, group, and search across everything.
- A Nominee gap finder, so you can spot which accounts still need a beneficiary assigned.
- Break Glass, a dedicated emergency section for your family, documents, and key contacts, readable by them when it matters most.
- Encrypted backup and restore, including full disaster recovery onto a brand new Mac.
- Change your master password anytime, right from Settings, with zero data loss.
- Bank-grade security throughout: AES-256-GCM encryption, master password with Touch ID, auto lock, screenshot and screen recording protection, and an instant privacy cover.
- A calm, premium liquid glass design with native macOS vibrancy, in both light and dark mode.

Built for any family, anywhere

Fully customizable account types, institution types, and currency, Indian Rupee, US Dollar, Euro, British Pound, and more, each with the right number formatting. Comes with sensible defaults out of the box, but every list reshapes to fit how your family, in any country, actually manages money.

Your data, your Mac, your rules. No cloud. No tracking. No compromises.

1. IN
Dictate in Spanish or English or paste the markdown text you wanna format/use somewhere else.

2.SHAPE
Say "heading", "bullet" or "task" while you're talking and the structure appears as you speak — or press a key instead, if your hands are already there. Say it the way you want to read it.

Pause as long as you need to think. Pick it up again when you've got it. It stays the same document until you decide it's finished. And it never rewrites your words — it only shapes them.

3-OUT
Then pick where you're pasting, and the same capture comes out correct for that place.


Key Features:

🔛 Transcribe speech in real time 

🗣️ Structure as you speak (headings, lists, checkboxes, quotes and code), with no syntax to remember and nothing to tidy up afterwards

🖱️ Paste formatted text back into any app with one click

7️⃣ One capture, seven destinations (Markdown, Social, Slack, HTML rich text, JIRA, plain text and outline). Slack gets single asterisks. Gmail gets real rich text. LinkedIn gets Unicode, because LinkedIn has no formatting at all; etc, etc.

📄 Already have the text? Paste it in and reformat it with your voice (particularly useful for whatever an AI just handed you)

🇪🇸🇬🇧 Dictate in Spanish or English 

📝 Edit structure or format at any time — reclassify any line as a heading, bullet, task or quote, or add/remove bold and italic, after you've already spoken it

🔍 Access your capture history anytime to find and reuse past recordings, nd re-exportable to a different format whenever you need it

apps.name: Crates
apps.tagline: Crate-dig the internet's audio
apps.description:
Crates helps you find interesting sounds. Whether you're a music maker looking for unique samples or just a curious sound explorer, Crates helps you find something new.

📖 HOW TO USE CRATES

Start by describing the vibe you're after — something like "dusty soul grooves" — then hit Dig. Crates heads out to Archive.org and uses your search to find sounds in that general vicinity, then automatically plays through short snippets of tracks: jumping to a random point within each recording, playing for a few seconds, then fading into the next sound. Turn off Auto-flip if you want to stay on one track instead of continuously advancing.

❤️ SAVE YOUR FAVOURITES

If you hear something you like, hit the Save icon to add it to your crate. If you miss saving something, or just want to jump back, use the Queue or transport controls to move backwards and forwards through what's played — your full session history is kept, so you can always find your way back.

📦 EXPLORE YOUR FINDS

Once you've built up a collection, click the Crate icon to open your library. From here you can listen back to what you saved — playback starts from the exact point you first heard it. Click the external link icon to visit that recording's page on Archive.org and explore further. Each recording displays its relevant copyright info as you browse.

🔍 SEARCH FILTERS

Want to keep things fully open? Turn on Creative Commons filtering in the search bar to only surface CC-licensed material — with an option to exclude non-commercial and no-derivatives licenses too. Prefer to search without AI assistance? You can turn that off too.

💽 RECORD YOUR STREAM

Click the Record button in the toolbar to capture the stream's output. Choose your save location and file format (M4A, MP3, or WAV) in Settings.

⌨️ SHORTCUTS

Use spacebar to play/pause and the arrow keys to skip forward and back. Click the "?" icon any time for a quick refresher on how it all works.

aiCapability.purpose: Interprets your typed style keywords into tuned Archive.org searches for finding sounds.

- Replay Canvas — an infinite memory space. Your projects, apps, collections, chapters and moments laid out as a landscape you can pan and zoom, tied by the connections already in your history. Focus a memory to see its network, or let the camera tour it.
- Timeline — your history read at any depth, with layers you toggle on their own: sessions, projects, bookmarks, notes, reflections, moments, and more.
- Story & Chapters — your days narrated back in plain sentences, your history divided into the eras it naturally fell into, and an autobiography told a week, a month, or a year at a time — every sentence drawn only from what you actually did.
- Museum, Collections & Projects — the best of your history, gathered; the kinds of work you do; and the app combinations that keep recurring, yours to name.
- Reflections — jot what you'd like to remember about a day, and it becomes part of your record.
- Calm by design: soft materials, gentle motion, generous space, and native macOS throughout — keyboard shortcuts, context menus, and a menu-bar mode. Nothing is gamified, nothing is scored, and a quiet day is never a failure.
- Private, always: your timeline lives in a single database file in your own user folder. Export it, back it up, or erase it entirely — the choice is only ever yours. Replay needs no special permissions to run, and your day never leaves this computer.

apps.name: Foldery
apps.tagline: Launch folders in your favorite app
apps.description:
Foldery — Launch folders in your favorite app

Stop digging through Finder. Foldery gives every project folder a home — and one click to open it in exactly the tool you need, whether that's your IDE, your terminal, or your file manager.

Save once, launch anywhere

Drop a folder into Foldery and assign it to one or more apps — PhpStorm, PyCharm, Warp, VS Code, ForkLift, iTerm, and more. From then on, opening that folder is a single click away, no matter which app you actually need it in today.

Built for how developers really work

- Multiple apps per folder — open the same project in your IDE and your terminal at once, or pick just one
- Groups — organize folders by client, project, or however makes sense to you
- Favorites— pin the folders you live in every day; favorited folders show their app's icon at a glance, so you know exactly what you're opening before you click
- Recents — your most recently opened folders, tracked automatically, no setup required
- Multi-select everywhere — add several folders at once, move them between groups in bulk, or batch-open a whole set in one app
- Quick-open command palette — hit a global shortcut, type a few letters, and jump straight to any folder without touching your mouse
- Drag and drop — the fastest way in: drag a folder from Finder onto Foldery and pick where it opens

Why not just use "Open With"?

Most developer tools don't register themselves as folder handlers with macOS, so they never show up in Finder's Open With menu. Foldery skips that limitation entirely — it launches your apps directly, so anything installed on your Mac becomes a one-click destination.

Perfect for:

- Developers juggling multiple projects across different IDEs and terminals
- Anyone who opens the same folders in different tools depending on the task
- Teams standardizing how they jump between JetBrains apps, VS Code, and terminal emulators

Save a folder once. Open it anywhere, every time.

Want even sharper names? Turn on Enhanced Naming in Settings, and Grove can tap into built-in AI for richer, more precise filename suggestions when you're online,  no API key, no setup. It's entirely optional: Grove's on-device naming works great on its own, offline, forever.  Enhanced Naming is just there for when you want that extra bit of precision.

Everything lives inside your chosen Space, mirrored in a real "Grove" folder on your Mac desktop, so you always know exactly where your organized files are and can point any other app straight to them.

100% private, 100% on-device
Every rename, every scan, every sort happens right on your Mac. No account required, no cloud, nothing uploaded ever. Grove works completely offline, by design.

Cleanup that feels good
Archive or delete clutter in one click, resolve duplicates instantly, and never worry about losing something nothing is ever deleted automatically.

See your month, beautifully
Generate a Grove Wrap anytime:  a real, personal recap of everything you organized, ready to save and share.

Hit the download buttton and Let Grove tend to your files.

Key Features:

Rhyme coloring — each block's rhyming end-words are tinted with one of 6 cycling colors; the letter badge matches, so you see at a glance which lines rhyme 
Internal rhyme / near-rhyme — words that echo within a line (shared end-sound, assonance, or consonance) get a light dotted underline, distinct from the colored end-rhyme highlight.

Meter marks — small dots above each word show heuristic stressed (filled) vs. unstressed (faint) syllables to match cadence.

Length check — a line's syllable count turns amber (with a hover note) when it's 30%+ off its block's average.

Repetition & clichés — a new Analysis tab lists overused words with counts (click one to search rhymes) and softly nudges on common cliché pairs (it flagged "heart / apart" and "fire / desire" in the test).

Persistence/autosave 

Song library — sidebar lists songs with metadata subtitle; create/rename/delete/switch present.

Metadata bar — Key / BPM / Genre above the editor.

Version history + Export + Copy + Focus — toolbar has Save version, Version history, Copy to clipboard, Export song, and Focus-mode toggle (plus sidebar/inspector toggles)

Tag palette — 10 tag chips ([Verse]…[Ad-lib]) plus custom-tag input.

Structure navigator — the Structure tab lists detected sections (Intro, Verse 1, Pre-Chorus, Chorus…) with line counts and avg syllables/line (e.g. 11.0, 4.3), with 21 clickable jump links.

Tempo density 

Datamuse modes — query-mode dropdown ("Perfect rhymes" + the 5 others).

Result filters — syllable-count and part-of-speech ("Any syllables" / "Any type").

Word Bank — pinnable per-song favorites section.

Rhythm Heat Map — a thermometer toggle in the editor toolbar overlays color onto your lyrics during revision (auto-hidden in the distraction-free drafting mode, and it skips [tags] and ALL-CAPS cues):
Gray line — "sleep" warning: natural rhythm perfectly matches a rigid metric pattern.
Red words — rhythm-forcing: archaic contractions ('tis, 'neath, 'twas), filler "do" ("when stars do shine"), and grammatical inversions ("came the dawn").
Yellow words — confusion: a bare noun likely missing an article or pronoun.
Green words — vitality: a tasteful substitution against the meter (e.g. a trochee opening an iambic line).

Rhythm tab (Critic's Study) — diagnostic counts for each of the four above, plus a Living Speech panel (archaic words, exhausted clichés like "red as a rose", and ponderous polysyllables to trade for short Anglo-Saxon words), and a toggleable Best Practices reference.

Assonance & Consonance search — the rhyme dictionary now has a dedicated "Assonance (vowel echo)" mode and a relabelled "Consonance" mode for off-rhymes that expand your vocabulary beyond strict end-rhymes.

Visual Daily & Weekly Schedules
Drag-and-drop timeline or card-based builder with your family’s real routines. Includes morning activities like outside walks, bus/CNG rides, gym ball jumping with counting (1-2-3), hand massage, hanging in the air, straw drinking, straw/balloon exercises, sensory breaks, and more.

Add custom steps with timers, First/Then boards, personal notes (“Count out loud during jumps”), and flexible variations so you can “break routine sometimes” without stress.

Interactive check-offs, progress bars, visual timers, and gentle transition warnings help reduce anxiety and build independence.

Personal Photos & Customization
Attach real local photos to any step (your exact gym ball, front door, kitchen straw, etc.). 

Personalized photos are especially effective for kids with autism and ADHD. Toggle between photos, symbols (ARASAAC-style), or text to match your child’s level.

Occupational Therapy & Progress Tracking
Session logger for therapist notes, activities completed, missed sessions, and suggested home practice. Track skill stages in motor, speech, sensory regulation, and more.

Visual charts and milestone checklists show progress over days/weeks/months. Export clean, anonymized PDF or JSON summaries for therapists, transparently showing what worked, what couldn’t be done, and where more support is needed.

Co-Parent Collaboration (Local Sharing)
“Share with Co-Parent” button for easy export/import of routines, schedules, OT notes, progress, and reflections as a single file.

Send via AirDrop, USB, or Messages. Smart merging supports both parents suggesting and editing routines. Handover notes keep you and your wife perfectly in sync (“Skipped straw exercise today — try after dinner”). 

No cloud required, everything stays fully private and local.Sensory, Mood & Independence Supports
Quick pre/post activity sensory/mood checker.

Optional gentle reinforcement and reward visuals.
Independence tracking (full/partial/independent prompts) with suggestions for fading support over time.

Simplified child-friendly view with voice feedback for growing self-use.Community Insights (Local-First)
Local library of anonymized routine templates and parent tips (e.g., “Straw exercises helped oral motor for many families” or strategies for hyperactivity during transitions). 

Import/export your own templates to learn from and share with other parents via files no central server. Design & Privacy

Beautiful, Apple-style calm interface with soft colors, high contrast options, large touch-friendly elements, reduced motion toggle, and accessibility features (voice feedback, large fonts, keyboard shortcuts).

Multi-profile support. Fully offline, airplane-mode compatible. All data stored locally in privacy-focused files (JSON/SQLite). Easy backup/export. 

No accounts, no tracking, nothing leaves your device.This is not a medical diagnosis or treatment tool it is a practical daily companion that helps parents create predictable routines, track real-life habits, reduce overwhelm, and support evidence-based approaches like visual supports, task analysis, positive reinforcement, and naturalistic strategies. 

Research shows these tools help build executive function, independence, and calmer days for neurodivergent children when used consistently alongside professional therapy.Made with love by a parent who gets it. Start with one morning routine and watch small consistent steps make a big difference on this lifelong journey.

PromptPocket floats above your other apps, remains available across every Space (including full-screen apps), and keeps the content you reach for most always within easy reach—without constantly switching between Notes, documents, old conversations, browser tabs, or AI chats.

Copy text to your clipboard with a single click, paste directly from the clipboard into an empty node, launch saved URLs in your browser, dictate ideas with your voice, reorder nodes by dragging them into the perfect sequence, or color-code important items for quick visual scanning.

Keep your most useful information close at hand, move it in and out with minimal friction, and stay focused on your work instead of searching for the same text again and again.

apps.name: Flor

apps.description:
Flor helps you build a more balanced view of your workdays through quick, proactive check-ins.

Whether you’re a founder, freelancer, creator, student, or knowledge worker, it’s easy to let one difficult moment define your entire day. Flor captures small moments throughout your workday, helping you see the bigger picture instead of relying on memory alone.

During your working hours, Flor gently asks short questions about your mood, focus, energy, progress, and friction. Each check-in takes only a few seconds. Over time, your responses are transformed into a visual calendar that reveals how your days and weeks actually unfolded.

Designed to be private

Unlike many modern apps, Flor doesn’t use AI or cloud services. Your responses are never sent to external servers or used to train models.

Everything is stored locally on your Mac, giving you a private space to reflect on your workday with complete control over your data.

Features

• Proactive check-ins throughout your workday
• Questions about mood, energy, focus, progress, and friction
• Complete each check-in in just a few seconds

Choose the mode that fits how you speak:

TELEPROMPTER MODE

Add a script and read at your own pace. ACE follows your voice and keeps your current lines in view.

COPILOT MODE

Describe what you want to talk about, then speak naturally. ACE understands the context and generates helpful next sentences in real time.

KEYWORDS MODE

List the key points you want to cover. As you mention each one, ACE automatically marks it as covered.

PRESENTER MODE

Connect your Keynote presentation and let ACE follow your slide notes. It automatically advances to the next slide when you finish speaking.

ACE sits near your camera by default, helping you maintain more natural eye contact. You can resize it by dragging the edges, move it anywhere on your screen, switch to Window mode, and use the built-in timer to stay on schedule.

Customize the experience in Settings with different themes, text alignment, fonts, text sizes, and opacity. You can also hide ACE while screen sharing, so your audience only sees what you want to present.

After each session, review a summary of your speaking time, pace, and progress.

Whether you are presenting, recording, interviewing, teaching, or speaking live, ACE helps you remember what comes next and focus on what you want to say.

apps.name: Switchyard
apps.tagline: X-ray of your dev workspace
apps.description:
Your coding environment is more than a repository. It is a web of agents, instructions, skills, MCP servers, environment requirements, Git state, development processes, ports, and project context. Switchyard brings that web into one clear, workspace-first view.

Open a project folder and Switchyard builds a local map of the systems around it. See which agents are available, which instructions and skills apply, how tools are configured, whether required environment names are present, what has changed in Git, and which local processes and ports belong to the Workspace. Evidence and confidence labels distinguish verified configuration from observed or inferred connections.

A portfolio view keeps your approved repositories organized with stack summaries, health signals, recent activity, pins, favorites, and tags. Workspace views connect configuration, context, runtime, and history, while Agent Activity summarizes supported local session metadata without turning Switchyard into another IDE or terminal.

Switchyard is local-first and read-only by default. You choose which roots it can inspect and which discovery sources are enabled. Secret values and message content are not displayed or persisted; supported session sources are parsed locally for allowlisted metadata. Optional MCP health checks are disclosed before making outbound requests, and unsupported or unavailable sources are labeled instead of being filled with guesses.

Whether you are opening an unfamiliar repository, resuming active work, or checking the state of projects across your Mac, Switchyard helps you see how the pieces connect before you hand control to an agent.

apps.name: Aside
apps.tagline: Put it aside. Pick up when it matters.
apps.description:
Aside is a calm, lightweight macOS utility for the things that interrupt your work but do not need your attention right now.
A link you want to revisit. A file you need tomorrow. A piece of text you do not want to lose. An image, thought, or reference that matters — just not at this exact moment.
With Aside, you can park it in seconds and get back to what you were doing.
Open Aside from the menu bar or with a global keyboard shortcut, add the item, choose when it should return, and move on. When the time is right, Aside brings it back with the context you saved.
Unlike a task manager, Aside does not ask you to organize your life, create projects, assign priorities, or maintain another list. It is a temporary holding space for digital objects that need to wait.
Your parked items are stored locally inside Aside’s private Context Vault. Original files stay exactly where they are and are never moved, renamed, or changed. Aside keeps a safe snapshot when needed, along with the useful context around it: what it is, why it mattered, and when you want it back.
For an extra layer of support, the optional Remember the context feature can suggest a clearer title, a short context note, and a suitable return time. AI is always opt-in, only runs when you ask for it, and never changes the original content.
Aside is designed to stay out of the way:
Quick access from the menu bar
Global keyboard shortcut
Support for text, links, files, images, and clipboard content
Flexible return times
Local-first storage
Optional AI context suggestions
Full keyboard navigation
VoiceOver support
Reduce Motion support
No account required
No projects, priorities, streaks, or productivity scores.

Aside gives your attention somewhere to set things down.
Not forever. Just until they matter again.

Every note is stored locally as a standard Markdown file.

How does it work? Easy!

1. Launch Cling.
2. Open the webpage, document, or file you are working with.
3. Press 'Command + N' to create a new sticky note.
4. Press 'Tab' to link the note to that source.
5. Click the paperclip icon in the note’s top bar to enable contextual display.
6. Switch to another window, then return to the linked source. The note will appear when its source is in focus and disappear when it is not.

Supported sources currently include: Safari, Chrome, and other Chromium-based browsers · All local files · Microsoft Office · iWork · Adobe Creative Cloud · Visual Studio Code · Xcode · Figma · Affinity · Final Cut Pro · DaVinci Resolve · Obsidian · Notion

apps.name: Kip

apps.description:
This is my very cool app for my very uncool saved-articles graveyard.

How many times have you read an article thinking, “I should remember this”, « I should keep that article somewhere"?

Now be honest: how many do you remember of? how many articles you saved have you reopened? 

Kip turns anything worth remembering into flashcards and save the source — with one shortcut.

Highlight it, press ⌥K and keep reading. Kip captures the source, generates the cards and schedules their reviews with spaced repetition.

Without active review, we forget up to 90% of what we read within a week. Spaced repetition brings each card back when it needs attention, so you achieve the best time spent/retained knowledge ratio. 

- Capture in one keystroke
 Highlight something valuable and press ⌥K (or whatever shortcut you want!). Kip saves it and starts making cards.

- Generate cards locally
On supported Macs, Apple Intelligence creates flashcards entirely on-device and private. You can also use Glaze AI, especially if you feel more confident with more powerful AI models. 

- Keep the full source at the same time without any additional work
Cards remain attached to their original source, so you can always return to the full context.

- Review at the right time
Kip schedules each card based on how well you remember it. Study what is due, then get on with your day.

- Stay in control
Review every generated question and answer. Edit it, delete it, or add your own cards.

- See what needs attention
Due counts, source-level progress and an activity heatmap make your next obvious.

The basic user flow is:

  1. Read something useful.
  2. Capture it with ⌥K, or paste the source into Kip (use the shortcut it’s cooler).
  3. Review the generated cards.
  4. Spend a few focused minutes on what is due.
  5. Good job!

- Dark and light modes
- No complicated deck setup

apps.name: Halo

Halo is a macOS menu bar accessory that puts system controls and shortcuts at the edges of your screen. Move your cursor into a corner or along an edge and a compact overlay appears: scrub volume, change brightness, launch apps, run a Shortcut, check what’s playing, start a focus timer, or pull up whatever else you’ve mapped there. It stays out of the Dock and lives in the tray until you need it.

What you can customize
Every display gets its own layout of four corners and four edges. Each zone can be turned off or assigned a role:

Volume, brightness, keyboard backlight
Appearance (light/dark), mute, keep awake
Now Playing (Apple Music / Spotify: seek, play/pause, skip)
Quick Dock (up to eight pinned apps)
Action (macOS Shortcut, open an app, open a URL, or run a script under your home folder)
System stats (CPU and memory)
Ask AI (summarize what’s on screen)
Focus Timer (Pomodoro-style focus and break cycles)
Corners use a dial. Edges use a bar that sits flush against the screen. Toggles are a tap. Media and the focus timer get their own controls.

In Settings you can:

Pick roles per corner and edge, per display
Tune hot zone size and how sticky the hide behavior feels
Build a Quick Dock and reorder or replace apps
Create app profiles so the frontmost app swaps dock apps and/or zone roles (e.g. a coding layout vs a writing layout)
Set Focus Timer lengths: focus, short break, long break, and how many cycles before a long break
Turn haptics and interface sounds on or off
Recalibrate spacing relative to the menu bar, Dock, and notch
Everything else
Halo walks you through the corners and edges on first launch, then drops you into Hot Zones settings. Hold Control-Shift-H to temporarily disable every hot zone when you need a clean shot at the menu bar clock, a window’s close button, or anything else sitting on an edge. Accessibility permission is required for the system controls; Settings shows whether you’re allowed and can send you to Privacy settings if not.

It runs as a quiet accessory: amber tray icon, optional timer status in the menu while a focus session is going, no Dock tile unless Settings is open. The look is intentionally flat and restrained: dark plate, amber accent, no noisy chrome.

apps.name: MoveBro

apps.description:
MoveBro

A calm, local-first Mac app for no-equipment home workouts.

MoveBro helps you move your body in short, guided bursts throughout the day — no gym, no gear, no account, and no internet required. Everything runs privately on your Mac.

What it does

- Guided workout sessions — Follow along with looping visual demos for each move, a big countdown timer (or rep counter), automatic rest phases, and one-line form cues so you always know what to do next. Pause, skip, or quit anytime.
- Plans for any amount of time — Choose from curated built-in plans (from a 5-minute quick energizer up to a full ~1-hour endurance session) or build your own custom plan.
- Gentle daily reminders — Set fixed times for a full workout, plus optional interval "nudges" that suggest a quick micro-set every few hours while your Mac is on. Notifications let you start right away or snooze 30 minutes.
- Start without opening the app — A menu-bar leaf icon and a global hotkey (⌘⇧M) launch a quick micro-session in a compact window — no need to open the full app.
- Stay motivated — A streak counter tracks your consistency with a forgiving "grace rule" (one missed day a week won't break your streak), and each session ends with a calm completion summary.
- Move together — "Start together" lets you pick a plan and a clock time so you and someone else begin in sync with a shared 3-2-1 countdown.
- Make it yours — Settings for theme, sound on/off and chime choice, reminder times, and more.

How it helps you

MoveBro removes every excuse and every bit of friction around home exercise. There's nothing to buy, set up, or log into — open it and move. The short sessions and interval nudges make it easy to stay active during a busy workday, the guided demos and cues mean you never have to wonder if you're doing it right, and the calm, glassmorphism design makes exercising feel like a peaceful break rather than a chore. Because it's fully offline and private, your activity stays entirely on your own Mac.

apps.name: Stellata
apps.tagline: Explore the universe in 3D
apps.description:
Stellata is a browser-based 3D model of the universe that you fly through. It places over 330,000 real stars and objects: the Solar System's planets and moons, hundreds of thousands of nearby stars and multiple-star systems, the interstellar dust and molecular clouds between them, the Milky Way, and the nearest galaxies. Every object is placed from published astronomical observation; nothing is invented or procedurally generated. Everything is shown in true colour and at the apparent brightness your eyes would actually see from any point in space: no infrared, radio, or false-colour imagery.

The model simulates what it would actually look like to move through the universe. Variable stars pulsate at their catalogue periods, close binaries orbit on their measured elements, and every star advances from its catalogue epoch to the present along its measured motion in space. It is not a theoretical or artistic rendering: every object comes from published astronomical observation and direct, empirical measurement.

Data source citations:

- AT-HYG v3.3 (https://codeberg.org/astronexus/athyg): David Nash's combined Tycho-2 / Hipparcos / Gaia catalogue — the star backbone.
  - Bailer-Jones et al. 2021 (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/abd806): geometric distances from Gaia DR3 parallaxes.
  - Edenhofer et al. 2024 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8187943): 3D dust extinction map of the local Milky Way.
  - Frisch & Slavin 2013 (https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-082312-140843): solar apex direction through the local ISM.
  - Gaia DR3 (https://gea.esac.esa.int/archive/): ESA / DPAC — raw astrometry, astrophysical parameters (Teff, log g, [M/H]), and non-single-star orbits.
  - GCVS 5.1 (http://www.sai.msu.su/gcvs/gcvs/): Samus et al. — variable-star periods.
  - Hipparcos CCDM (https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/cat/I/239): ESA — HIP double-star cross-match.
  - IAU WGCCRE (Archinal et al. 2018) (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10569-017-9805-5): planet and moon axial tilt and rotation.
  - JPL Solar System Dynamics (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sats/elem/): mean orbital elements for the 18 major moons.
  - JPL Standish 1992 (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html): planet positions (Keplerian elements).
  - Local Volume Database (Pace 2024): dwarf-galaxy parameters.
  - Mallama, Krobusek & Pavlov 2018 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.icarus.2016.09.023): V-band albedos and phase curves.
  - McConnachie 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-6256/144/1/4): Local Group positions, distances, and luminosities.
  - Multiple Star Catalog (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4365/aaa7d9): Tokovinin 2018 (Pulkovo) — hierarchical subsystem orbits.
  - NASA planetary fact sheets (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/): radii and mean elements; Pluto from New Horizons 2015.
  - SIMBAD (https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/): CDS Strasbourg — cross-identifications and catalogue validation.
  - Sixth Orbit Catalog (ORB6) (http://www.astro.gsu.edu/wds/orb6.html): USNO — computed visual orbits.
  - Stellarium (https://github.com/Stellarium/stellarium): constellation lines.
  - Voyager 1 & 2 (https://voyager.jpl.nasa.gov/): boundary crossings (2012, 2018), plus IBEX / Cassini ENA heliotail estimates.
  - Washington Double Star Catalog (http://www.astro.gsu.edu/wds/): USNO — resolved pair geometry.
  - Zucker et al. 2020 & 2021 (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/ac1f96): molecular-cloud distances, 3D bounding boxes, and density profiles.

Source on GitHub: https://github.com/alexmensch/stellata
Full data source notes, modelling decisions, and project scope: https://github.com/alexmensch/stellata/blob/main/SCIENCE.md

Created by Alex Marshall, https://alxm.me

apps.name: Metadata Cleaner

I made Metadata Cleaner because I could not find a simple FOSS macOS app built around the mat2 workflow I trusted from Linux. Most Mac metadata-cleaning GUIs I found were built around ExifTool, while mat2 takes a more aggressive, format-aware approach to removing metadata from supported files.

Metadata Cleaner keeps the workflow simple: add files, inspect the metadata they contain, clean them, and save non-destructive .cleaned copies while leaving the originals untouched. It is free, open source, zero cloud, and designed to do one job well.

Inspired by the excellent Metadata Cleaner project from the Linux community:

apps.name: Stream
apps.tagline: Your day, remembered before you have to.
apps.description:
Stream is a calm response to the three apps most people juggle just to run their day. Instead of a calendar, a to-do list, and a journal fighting for attention, Stream holds everything in one chronological line: what's happening, what needs doing, and what actually happened, in the order it happened.

Capture is built for speed. A single hotkey opens a floating field from anywhere on your Mac, and a thought becomes a scheduled event, a task, or a quiet note without you ever picking a category or an app. Stream reads dates, times, places, and people straight out of plain language, so "lunch with Ben at 8pm at Dominoes" becomes a real event before you've finished the sentence.

Nothing here nags. Tasks that slip carry forward on their own, aging quietly instead of turning red, because missing things is normal life, not a failure. Categories let you see only what matters to the moment you're in, at work or at home, without deleting or losing anything you didn't need to see. Life goals like piano practice or daily pushups live in their own low-pressure lane, tracked by a simple gap since last time, with no streaks to break and no guilt to carry.

Every event and reminder lives in Apple's own Calendar and Reminders, synced in real time in both directions, so Stream is a better lens on your data, not another silo. And every evening, instead of staring at a blank page trying to remember what you did, Stream shows you the day already laid out, ready for you to add the one line of reflection that turns a schedule into a memory.

Stream doesn't ask you to be more productive. It asks you to carry less, remember more, and end the day with something worth looking back on.

apps.name: SupaKey
apps.tagline: More shortcuts, more modifier keys!
apps.description:
SupaKey

Turn any key into a Hyper key — a modifier your Mac doesn't have.

macOS gives you four modifiers: ⌘ ⌃ ⌥ ⇧. SupaKey adds a fifth. Hold Caps Lock (or any key you choose) and press another key to trigger ⌘⌃⌥⇧ shortcuts — a combination no app uses, so your shortcuts never conflict with anything. Tap it quickly and it acts as Escape, Caps Lock, or whatever you pick.

What you can do with it:

Hyper shortcuts - bind Caps Lock + any key in any app's shortcut settings as ⌘⌃⌥⇧+key
Custom keys - sacrifice a key (F13, numpad, etc.) to act as an extra Hyper modifier, with optional tap-to-passthrough
Launch & focus apps - Caps Lock + key launches an app, focuses it, or hides it
Run Shortcuts.app - trigger HomeKit, Focus modes, and automations
Shell commands & text snippets - run a script or type canned text at the cursor
Screenshots - capture a window, screen, or area straight to clipboard
System actions - toggle dark mode, lock screen, sleep display, empty trash
Exceptions - disable the SuperKey in specific apps like games or terminals
Built on macOS native tech - no driver required. Uses the system's own key remapping (hidutil) plus a lightweight event tap (the same technique Hammerspoon uses). One Accessibility permission and you're set.

Books
A simple ledger of income and expenses with categories, filters, and tool tags editable after import so your books stay accurate.

Tool Guard
Set monthly budgets for AI and other tools. Spend comes from linked expenses (imports can tag vendors like OpenAI, Cursor, and Claude). Progress bars show healthy / near limit / over. The Adviser adds transparent Keep / Watch / Cut guidance when tools stack or run hot visibility, not auto-cancel.

Recovery
Track refunds and disputes (status, amounts, deadlines). On import or via Scan for recoveries Mamori suggests matches from refund/chargeback language and credits that pair with earlier charges. You always confirm before anything is added; nothing is filed with your bank.

Watch critical URLs with simple uptime checks and notices. Export accountant-friendly CSVs and a base-currency P&L, including currency and converted amounts where it matters.

Privacy
Data stays on your Mac. Built for one operator: local, offline-friendly, honest about rates and suggestions no crypto theater, no enterprise finance suite.

It doesn't just list data — it interprets it. Security headers are graded A+ to F with copy-ready Nginx fixes for every issue found. Expiring domains and certificates trigger warnings before they become outages.
Every scanned URL lands in the sidebar with its grade badge. Click any entry to reopen its report, hit Re-scan to check it again, and switch between historical snapshots of the same site. Instant search keeps even a long history usable. Reports export to Markdown or JSON.

Open a window.
Show a dock icon.
Store anything, anywhere, ever.
Care what the text says.

apps.name: Activity Ridge
apps.tagline: The activity journal that writes itself.
apps.description:
Activity Ridge
The activity journal that writes itself.

Activity Ridge shows you what you did on your Mac over the last thirty days.

It can do this on the first launch, before it has ever run in the background, because it doesn't watch you. Everything it shows comes from records your Mac already keeps. The timestamps on your files. The commits in your git repositories. The history databases your browser and apps write to disk. That material was already sitting there. Ago reads it and lays it out.

Open the app and you get a single day. At the top, a line of text saying what you made and how many hours you were active. Below that, a shape: two ridges spread across the hours of the day. The green ridge is what you made, meaning files you created and commits you wrote. The grey ridge behind it is where the time went, meaning the sites and apps you spent time in, the screenshots you took, the things you downloaded. Under the shape, the specifics. Commit messages. Filenames. The apps you spent longest in.

Arrow keys move between days. Escape opens the month: thirty small versions of the same shape, so you can see the shape of a month at once. Click any day to open it.

What it reads

File creation and modification times in Desktop, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Movies, and your code folders.
Commits authored by you in git repositories on this Mac, including the commit message.
Browser and app history, reduced to the domain or app name and how long you were there.

What it does not do

It does not record your screen. It does not log keystrokes. It does not read the contents of your files. It stores no URLs and no page titles, only domains. It makes no network requests of any kind, so nothing leaves the machine, and there is no account and nothing to sign into. Each of the three sources can be switched off in settings, and turning one off removes it from every view immediately.

What it can and cannot see

Activity Ridge sees work that leaves a trace on disk. Writing code, editing documents, taking screenshots, browsing, committing. It cannot see work that leaves none, so a day spent reading paper or in a meeting off your calendar will look quieter than it was. It is a record of what your machine touched, not a timesheet.

apps.name: SEOInspector

apps.description:
SEOInspector — SEO analysis that starts free and scales with real data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
SEOInspector is a macOS app for auditing and researching SEO, built around one simple idea: some checks need real search data, and some don't. So it's split cleanly in two.                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Works instantly, no account needed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Seven checks run entirely on your Mac, analyzing pages directly — no API key, no sign-up, no cost:                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
- On-Page SEO Audit — crawls a page and runs over 100 checks across meta tags, headings, links, structured data, accessibility, and technical SEO, plus automatic tech-stack detection (CMS, analytics, CDN, server).                                                                                            
- SERP Snippet Preview — see exactly how a page will look as a Google search result and as a shared social card, with warnings for missing titles, oversized descriptions, noindex tags, and missing preview images.                                                                                             
- Structured Data Validator — finds every JSON-LD block on a page, checks it parses, and shows which schema.org types it declares.                                                                                                                                                                               
- Robots.txt Tester — checks whether a specific URL is allowed or blocked for Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, or any crawler you choose.                                                                                                                                                                             
- Redirect Checker — follows the full redirect chain for a batch of URLs and reports final status codes, ideal before a site migration.                                                                                                                                                                          
- Sitemap Checker — parses sitemap indexes and URL sets (including gzipped sitemaps), then verifies a sample of URLs for status codes and robots.txt blocking.                                                                                                                                                   
- Hreflang Checker — verifies that every hreflang alternate links back to the original page, catching the most common real-world hreflang bug.  

Bring your own DataForSEO API key for live search data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Nine more checks are powered by real, live SEO data from DataForSEO — the industry data provider behind many SEO tools. To use them, you'll need your own DataForSEO API key: create a free account at DataForSEO, generate an API key, and add it in SEOInspector's Settings (it's encrypted and stored only on your Mac — never synced anywhere).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
DataForSEO's API is pay-as-you-go, not a subscription — there's no monthly fee to DataForSEO itself, you're billed only for the requests you actually make. SEOInspector calls the DataForSEO API directly with your key, with no proxy and no markup on top — you pay DataForSEO's own rates, nothing more.     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
That makes SEOInspector a lighter-weight, pay-only-for-what-you-use alternative to subscription-based all-in-one platforms like Ahrefs or SEMrush: no locked-in monthly plan, no seat licenses — just a native Mac app plus usage-based API costs.                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   The nine data-backed checks:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
- Keyword Research — search volume, CPC, competition, keyword ideas, live SERP results, and optional AI search volume.                                                                                                                                                                                           
- Keyword Trends — compare search popularity for up to five keywords over time.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
- Domain Overview — a domain's estimated organic traffic, ranking keywords, top pages, and visibility trend over time.
- Keyword Cannibalization - find keywords where multiple pages on the same domain compete against each other.  
- Competitor Discovery - find domains competing with yours in search results - no need to already know their names.                                                                                                                                                                                         
- Backlinks — referring domains, full backlink profile, anchor text distribution, and link growth history.                                                                                                                                                                                                       
- Rank Tracker — track a domain's position for the keywords that matter to you, with historical trend charts.                                                                                                                                                                                                    
- LLM Mentions — see how often and where AI answer engines like ChatGPT mention your brand.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
- Brand Mentions — track mentions of a brand or keyword across the web, with sentiment and mentions-over-time.                                                                                                                                                                                                   
- Keyword Gap — compare two domains to find keywords a competitor ranks for that you don't.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
- Backlinks Gap — compare two domains' backlink profiles to find link-building opportunities.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Built to keep your API costs down                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
Every DataForSEO search is cached locally, so repeating the same search never bills you twice — a "Search again" button is always there when you actually want fresh data. Wherever possible, SEOInspector uses a single bulk API request instead of one call per item (for example, Rank Tracker checks an entire keyword list in one request, not one per keyword), keeping what you spend on DataForSEO lean by design.

apps.name: Meridian
apps.tagline: The Chinese organ clock for your Mac
apps.description:
Chinese medicine divides the day into twelve two-hour periods called shíchen. Each is governed by a different organ meridian, said to be at its peak during that window. The liver does its repair work around 2am. The stomach is at full strength at 8. The mind reaches a second, quieter peak in the late afternoon.

Meridian puts one character in your menu bar — the glyph for the hour you are currently in. Click it and you get what that hour is for: the organ at work, one sentence on what the body is doing, one thing worth doing, one thing worth avoiding. Below that, all twelve hours as a single strip, so you can see the shape of your day at a glance.

The colours in that strip repeat, and that is the point. Two hours share the same green because both are deep-focus windows. Two share gold because both are hours to ease off. Read left to right, the strip tells you where your focus windows sit and where the day is asking you to stop.

ON TRADITION, HONESTLY

This is a cultural framework, not a medical claim, and I have kept it deliberately conservative.

The popular “organ detox schedule” that circulates online is not found in the classical texts and is not supported by modern medicine. Meridian does not use it.

Where a traditional claim is experiential rather than verified — the idea that Qi rises to the brain in the late afternoon, for example — it stays what it is: a suggestion about when to schedule hard thinking, not a statement about physiology.

Nothing here diagnoses, treats, or prescribes anything.

What survives that pruning is still worth having: a very old, very specific opinion about when to eat, when to think hard, and when to stop. It is here because it is a good opinion, not because it is ancient.

WHY A MENU BAR APP

Most tools for your time help you fit more into a day. This one does the opposite. It comes out of a larger project of mine called RhythmOS, built on a single idea: don’t fill the day — put the right thing in the right hour.

Meridian is the smallest possible version of that idea. It does not manage your tasks, sync your calendar, or ask you to plan anything. It just tells you what hour it is, in a sense your calendar does not know about.

No account. No network requests. Nothing leaves your Mac. It works on a plane.

apps.name: BatteryPulse
apps.tagline: Real watts, measured. Not estimated.
apps.description:
BatteryPulse shows exactly how much power your Mac is
pulling from its battery, right now.

The number is measured, not estimated. BatteryPulse reads
instantaneous voltage and amperage directly from your
Mac's battery controller and refreshes every second — the
same source Activity Monitor's battery pane draws from,
surfaced as a figure you can actually read.

WHAT IT SHOWS
- Live power draw in watts, updating every second
- Time remaining, projected from a 60-second rolling
  average — with the wattage it's based on shown on
  screen, so you can check the math yourself
- A 30-minute discharge history that colors from green
  to red as your projected runtime falls
- Battery health, cycle count, temperature, voltage,
  and remaining capacity against full
- Optional background logging with CSV export, for when
  you want to find out what was actually running at 2pm

WHAT IT DOESN'T DO
macOS does not expose real per-app or per-peripheral
wattage — no sensor measures it, and any app showing you
"Chrome: 3.4W" is presenting a heuristic score dressed up
as a measurement. BatteryPulse doesn't do that. Every
number in this app is a real reading or arithmetic you
can verify on screen.

Every figure reconciles: divide remaining capacity by the
displayed average and you get the displayed time estimate.
Divide health's watt-hours and you get health's percentage.
That was the point.

All data stays on your Mac. Nothing is transmitted.
Requires a Mac with a built-in battery.

apps.name: Ghosted
apps.tagline: Ghost newsletters with a swipe
apps.description:
Your inbox is full of newsletters you never read. Ghosted helps you clear them out fast.

It looks through Mail on your Mac and finds everyone who keeps emailing you. Then it shows them one at a time, like a deck of cards.

Swipe right to keep them. Left to unsubscribe. Up to block and delete their emails. Down to decide later. Prefer buttons? They're right there too.

Most of the time you won't have to visit a website. Ghosted sends the unsubscribe for you and moves on to the next card. Only a few senders make you finish on their own page.

Blocking is stronger than unsubscribing. It deletes what they've already sent and stops anything new from reaching your inbox.

Nothing you do here gets uploaded. Your email stays on your Mac, and the only thing sent out is the unsubscribe itself.

Changed your mind? History shows everything you did. Unblock a sender, try an unsubscribe again if they ignored it, or bring someone back to decide later. You can also import/export history in settings.

Happy 👻

apps.name: Health Fusion
apps.tagline: Your Apple Health & WHOOP data, unified.
apps.description:
Health Fusion is a native macOS dashboard that brings your Apple Health and WHOOP data together in one place — no browser, no subscriptions, no cloud.

At a glance, every day 
The Overview gives you today's key metrics in a single view: steps, active calories, resting heart rate, HRV, recovery score, sleep duration, and strain. Charts show the past 7 or 30 days at a glance so you can spot patterns without digging.

Deep dives when you need them 
Dedicated sections for Apple Health and WHOOP let you explore each source in detail — heart rate trends, sleep stages, step history, HRV over time, recovery scores, strain, and a full workout log with per-session stats.

See what's connected 
The Correlations view plots your metrics against each other — sleep vs. HRV, strain vs. recovery, and more — with Pearson correlation coefficients and regression lines so you can understand what's actually driving your performance.

Sleep, done right 
Sleep is attributed to the morning you wake up, not the night you went to bed. Duplicate readings from iPhone and Apple Watch are automatically deduplicated. Apple Health and WHOOP sleep are merged, not stacked.

Your data stays on your Mac 
Apple Health data is imported from an export ZIP and parsed locally. WHOOP syncs directly via OAuth. Nothing leaves your machine.

Get started in minutes 
A built-in setup guide walks you through exporting from Apple Health and connecting WHOOP — step by step, with a demo mode if you want to explore before importing your own data.

Features

- Unified Overview with today's snapshot and 7/30-day charts
- Apple Health import (ZIP export, parsed locally)
- WHOOP OAuth sync with encrypted credential storage
- Steps, active calories, sleep, heart rate, HRV, recovery, strain, workouts
- Correlation scatter plots with regression lines
- Sleep stage breakdown and trends
- Workout log with per-session detail
- Dark mode, native macOS design
- Demo data mode — explore without importing anything

apps.name: Orb
apps.tagline: One orb. Every workspace. One click.
apps.description:
Orb turns "getting set up" into a single click.

Define a context Coding, Writing, Design, whatever your day is made of  and tell Orb what it should look like: which apps to open, which to hide or quit, exactly where each window goes (or full screen), your wallpaper, your browser tabs, your Focus mode. Then a floating orb lives quietly on your desktop. Click it, fan out your contexts, and your whole Mac rearranges itself in one motion.

Over time, Orb learns. It notices you always jump into Coding at 9am, that Design belongs on your second monitor, that you keep reopening Slack after it hides  and it adjusts. A gentle pulse suggests the switch; you decide. Ignore a suggestion three times and it stops asking.

No accounts. No cloud. No AI models phoning home. Every pattern Orb learns is stored on your Mac and yours to delete anytime. When you're done, one click returns you to a clean, neutral desktop with your original wallpaper.

Your work has modes. Now your Mac does too.

Feature bullets (if you need them)
One-click context switching apps, window layouts, full screen, wallpaper, tabs and Focus, all at once
A living desktop orb drag it anywhere, snaps to edges, fans out a radial menu of your contexts
Global hotkeys ⌥Space for the menu, or a shortcut per context for instant switching
Learns your routine, privately habit-aware suggestions that pulse, never pester; all on-device
Exit to a neutral space clean desktop, original (or custom) wallpaper, one click

Compare anything

Built for reviewing

Virtualized rendering that stays smooth at 16,000 lines. Line wrap and ignore-whitespace toggles. Drag-and-drop to start any comparison. Saved and recent comparisons. Command palette (⌘K), full keyboard shortcuts, and a native menu bar. Export or copy a unified .diff.

Ribbit Atelier is a real-time 3D jewelry studio built into the app. 12 stone families, 17 cuts, 16 engagement settings, 17 wedding band styles, six metals, nine finishes. Light actually bends through the stone — real refraction, dispersion, fire, opal play-of-color — so what you see is close to what a jeweler would hand you. Move the light anywhere with one control. Build the wedding stack next to the engagement ring. Then save a 4K portrait straight into your collection like any other ring.

- A little AI, only when you ask
Identify Details reads a ring's photo and product page and suggests the specs — you review before anything changes. Or describe your dream ring in a sentence and have Ribbit generate the image and fill in the details.

Fifteen real ring photographs are waiting on first launch, so there's something to look at before you've saved a thing.

apps.name: Just Now

Just Now holds the last five minutes of your screen and throws away everything older. It writes nothing down. Then something happens, you press one key, and it saves the five minutes that already went past.

It's built for the way people debug now: catch the bug on video, hand the file straight to your coding agent, and skip the part where you try to describe what you saw in words. The reproduction steps you could never remember are already in the recording.

Flexible destinations — sort files in place under their source folder, or route everything into shared destination folders that the AI picks between.
Batch sync — run a dry-run scan across existing files and approve a batch of proposed moves at once.
Full history & undo — every move is logged with the AI's reasoning, searchable, and reversible.
Drag-and-drop onto the tray icon — sort files or entire folders instantly without opening the app.

The main window shows a live countdown to your next break with a circular progress ring. When the break starts, it switches to a full look-away screen for a configurable duration. You can pause the timer, resume it, or trigger a break immediately at any time. It also tracks how many breaks you've taken versus skipped, and lets you reset those counters from the Settings panel.
Settings let you adjust two things: the interval between breaks (5 to 60 minutes, in 5-minute steps) and the break duration (10 to 60 seconds, in 5-second steps).

apps.description:
If you’re anything like me, your desktop slowly turns into a visual junk drawer of active files, project links, and shortcuts you need quick access to—until finding anything becomes a chore. 
I built Grid Dock to fix that exact problem and bring clean, structured focus back to macOS.

Grid Dock creates a sleek, floating grid overlay on your screen where you can keep your active tools, files, and links organized right at your fingertips without cluttering your desktop.

Why it makes a difference:

Tabbed Workspaces: Group your shortcuts into tabs by project or context (e.g., Client A, Development, Daily Ops). Switch contexts cleanly instead of searching through buried windows.

Universal Shortcuts: Drag and drop virtually anything into a cell—applications, local documents, scripts, or web URLs.

Seamless macOS Integration: Keep it floating above your workspace, call it up instantly with a custom global hotkey, or access it quietly from the Menu Bar.

Tailored to Your Look: Choose between Light, Dark, or System themes, and customize gridlines, icon sizes, and label styles (icon-only, text-only, or both) to match your ideal setup.

It’s lightweight, fast, and designed from the ground up to feel like a native part of Mac. Check it out and see how much smoother your workflow feels!

apps.name: News Flow
apps.tagline: One AI-ranked feed for news and video
apps.description:
News Flow gathers the day into a single feed - articles and video side by side, ranked by what you actually open, watch, and save. It starts working in the first minute: pick a few topics and languages, and the feed fills immediately while the AI learns the rest from how you read.

Every story opens in the app. Articles get a clean reader column; paywalled ones get a summary rather than a wall. Videos play in a floating window that stays above your other apps, with the comment thread beside it - and one right-click puts a comment in your own signed-in browser when you want to reply. Anything you save stays readable offline.

The morning starts with Today's Brief: the day in a handful of lines, each claim linked back to the story behind it, so you can check any of it in one click. When you have five minutes rather than fifty, filter by measured reading time. When you want to steer the feed, "more like this" and "hide" are one keystroke each.

Bring your own sources - any RSS feed, YouTube channel, or Bluesky account - and let the AI find relatives. Choose the engine that powers it: Glaze AI with no setup, a free Gemini key, OpenRouter, or Claude Code running locally on your own Mac.

aiCapability.purpose: Learns your interests from what you read and detects your language to rank the best news and videos for you.

Aegis is a local review workbench for Solidity projects. Open a Foundry or Hardhat repo and it maps the protocol surface, runs Slither plus focused Aegis checks when available, and turns detector output into prioritized review leads with source evidence, call-path context, confidence, assumptions, invalidation checks, and impact bounds.

It is built for pre-deploy triage: search and filter leads, jump to affected files, inspect connected calls, ask optional follow-up questions, and copy a structured Markdown report. If the companion engine is offline, Aegis falls back to an embedded local scanner so the workflow still works.

Aegis does not certify contracts as secure or replace a professional audit. It gives developers a clearer first pass before deeper manual review.

apps.name: Sigil
apps.tagline: Know which SSH key your Mac will use
apps.description:
As AI coding agents and automated developer tools take on a larger role in our day-to-day workflows, software security is shifting from a background concern to a frontline priority. Because agents execute code, manage environments, and push to repositories on our behalf, developers need complete clarity on how their local credentials are being accessed and used—especially when constantly juggling different personal and work SSH keys across multiple projects.

Sigil is a native, local-first macOS control panel built to bring total transparency to your Mac's SSH identity chain. Rather than acting as a custom agent or password manager, Sigil makes your existing system configuration instantly readable. Select any host to inspect its exact resolution path from SSH config rules and provider agents down to hardware protection states and public-key fingerprints. Sigil helps you verify you're authenticating with the right identity before pushing, spot configuration conflicts, catch missing key files, and confidently generate non-exportable, Secure Enclave–backed credentials protected by biometrics. Everything runs strictly on your Mac with zero cloud sync, remote connections, or telemetry, giving you full control over your work and personal profiles in an increasingly automated world.

Possible conversions:

- Documents — docx, doc, odt, rtf, txt, md, html, epub, ppt, xls, csv → PDF and between each other
- Audio/Video — mp3, wav, m4a, flac, mp4, mov, mkv, webm, avi, etc.; video→GIF; extract audio from video
- PDF toolkit — images→PDF, combine images/PDFs into one PDF, split PDF into pages, PDF→images, PDF→text

Data formats — JSON ↔ CSV ↔ TSV ↔ YAML ↔ XML (CSV also → XLSX/PDF)
- Plus: drag-and-drop or file picker, batch convert, Finder "Open With → Convert," and originals are never overwritten (always saved as a new file).

apps.name: Trace
apps.tagline: Screenshots organized, finally found
apps.description:
Your Mac doesn't have a screenshots folder. Every one you take lands on your Desktop, piles up, and quietly disappears into the mess. The receipt you'll need. The address someone sent. That color you saved. The text that made you laugh. All there somewhere, none of it findable.

Trace is the home they were missing.

It gathers every screenshot scattered across your Mac into one tidy place, then makes the whole thing searchable, not by filename, but by what's actually inside each image. Type "blue hex from Figma" or "that flight confirmation" and the exact screenshot surfaces in an instant. It reads the text in your screenshots right on your device, so finding anything feels a little like magic.

But Trace isn't a file manager. Your screenshots aren't clutter, they're a memory. The things you chose to hold onto. So Trace treats them that way: a warm, browsable wall of moments organized by when you captured them, the ones worth keeping just a tap away, and a gentle nudge to let go of the duplicates and one-time codes you'll never need again.

What Trace does:

Gathers loose screenshots from across your Mac into one home
Searches the text inside every screenshot, instantly
Organizes everything into a calm, beautiful timeline of moments
Keeps what matters close, and helps you gently let go of what doesn't
Auto-collects new screenshots the moment you take them

Private by design. Everything happens on your Mac. Your screenshots never leave your device. No cloud, no accounts, no exceptions.

Your screenshots have been trying to tell you something. Trace finally lets you find it.

apps.name: Scratch&&Sniff

It’s organized on a Kanban board for managing jobs across the 4 steps:

1. Scout - It crawls the domain and classifies links.
2. Review - Browse the results and decide which pages to keep or which you want to crawl more.
3. Collect - Capture fullpage screenshots and page content as markdown.
4. Export - Save all files and reports locally for use with Figma, Sheets, powerpoint, etc.


Some key features include:

- Uses your actual installed Chrome (not a bundled browser) for accurate, real-world rendering
- Automatic cookie-consent handling so banners don't clutter every screenshot
- Handles lazy-loading, animations, and sticky headers
- Visual site-map generation (tree and force-directed graph views)
- Re-run Scout or Collect with full versioning of prior results for comparison
- Jobs persist across sessions, so long-running research projects can be picked up later

Build your own food library with names, colors, and custom categories. Drag meals onto any day, move them between days, or organize them by breakfast, lunch, and dinner when you need finer control. When it is time to shop, open the weekly shopping list to see what you need. Ingredients from your planned meals are combined and totaled automatically; export the list as a text file or send it to Apple Notes in one step.

Your data stays on your Mac. Store it locally, or point the app at a folder in iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, or any synced location to keep your meal plan aligned across devices. Back up, restore, or move your data anytime with full export and import.

Key Features:
- Visual meal planning — eight-week rolling calendar with drag-and-drop assignment, move, and remove

- Flexible daily layout — optional breakfast, lunch, and dinner slots, or a single slot per day

- Personal food library — searchable sidebar with color-coded meals and custom categories

- Weekly shopping lists — aggregated ingredients across your plan, with export to text or Apple Notes

- Cloud-friendly storage — sync via your own folder, or keep everything on this device

- Backup & portability — export and import your full meal plan as JSON; change storage location with guided migration

Privacy-first by design: no sign-in, no server, no tracking — just your meal plan, stored where you choose.

apps.name: Markdown Ninja
apps.tagline: View And Work on Multiple MD Formats
apps.description:
Markdown Ninja is a native macOS app for reading, organizing, and polishing markdown — with full-fidelity rendering and one-click export to the tools you already use.

Browse your files like Finder, open several at once in tabs, and get GitHub-flavored markdown rendered exactly right: tables, task lists, math (KaTeX), syntax-highlighted code, and Mermaid diagrams, all in one clean, foldable view. Six markdown flavors are supported out of the box — .md, .markdown, .mdx, .mkd, .mdown, and .txt. YAML front matter is parsed and shown separately from the body, alongside live word/token/reading-time stats, so you always know what you're looking at without metadata cluttering your content.

Then take it anywhere. Export to PDF, Word, or HTML, or copy formatted markdown straight into Slack, Telegram, or Google Docs — no reformatting, no lost structure. Two built-in AI tools help you go further: translate any document into another language, or adjust its length to hit a target word/token count, both without leaving the app.

For power users, Markdown Ninja installs a mdninja command-line tool and an MCP server, so the same rendering, export, and AI features are scriptable from your terminal or usable directly by Claude Code, Codex, and other AI agents.

Highlights
* Full markdown rendering: GFM, math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax-highlighted code, inline HTML
* Multi-file tabs with a Finder-style sidebar and folder browser
* Export to PDF, HTML, or Word; copy formatted for Slack, Telegram, and Google Docs
* AI-powered translation and length adjustment, right from the toolbar
* Document stats: words, tokens, reading time, headings, links, images, and more
* Command-line tool (mdninja) and MCP server for scripting and AI-agent workflows
* Drag-and-drop file opening, Finder file-association support, and native vibrancy
* Light/Dark/System appearance with an in-app "What's New" changelog

aiCapability.purpose: Rewrites a markdown document to a target length or translates it into another language, preserving structure.

apps.name: Loci
